items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1971 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1971-04-15, assembled from Connacht (= 1957 boundaries), Leinster 1971, Munster 1971, Ulster (= 1963 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1977. In 1977, due to the expansion of Drogheda, part of the DED of St. Mary’s was ceded to County Louth by County Meath. Details on this can be found in the Local Government Provisional Order Confirmation Act, 1976. Also relevant is the renaming of An Uaimh to Navan on 25/06/1971, as its corresponding DEDs were renamed by 1971 Census Reports Volume 1 (published July 1972).

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1977 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1977-01-01, assembled from Connacht (= 1957 boundaries), Leinster 1977, Munster (= 1971 boundaries), Ulster (= 1963 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1983. In 1983 (following the expansion of Waterford county borough in 1980), Waterford's existing 24 wards were replaced by 38 new ones. 1 DED (Waterford Rural) was replaced, and 3 more (Ballinakill, Faithlegg, Kilbarry) were reduced in size. The following sources were used:

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1980 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1980-01-01, assembled from Connacht (= 1957 boundaries), Leinster (= 1977 boundaries), Munster 1980, Ulster (= 1963 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1977 with 3 DEDs split by the Waterford boundary extension (similar to how 14 EDs are split today by the 2019 Cork extension). Also relevant is the renaming of the following DEDs between 1979 Census Reports Volume 1 (published February 1980) and 1981 Census Reports Volume 1 (published September 1982): Bealanagarry to Bealanageary (Dunmanway R.D.) (Cork)

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1983 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1983, assembled from Connacht (= 1957 boundaries), Leinster (= 1977 boundaries), Munster 1983, Ulster (= 1963 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1985. In 1985, the DEDs of Blanchardstown, Coolock, Drumcondra Rural No. 1, Drumcondra Rural No. 2, Dundrum No. 1, Finglas and Palmerstown No. 1 and wards of Kimmage E, Pembroke East D and Rathfarnham D were split by the Dublin city boundary change.

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1986 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1986, assembled from Connacht 1986, Leinster 1986, Munster (= 1983 boundaries), Ulster (= 1963 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1994. In 1994, the boundaries of 9 DEDs and 4 wards were amended following the minor border changes to Dublin county borough and the counties (formerly electoral counties) of Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown, Fingal and South Dublin. I used the following sources to get the old boundaries:

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1994 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1994, assembled from Connacht (= 1986 boundaries), Leinster 1994, Munster (= 1983 boundaries), Ulster (= 1963 boundaries). Very slightly modified version of Electoral Divisions 1997. The difference between this and that map is that the electoral division of Cherry Orchard B was renamed to Carna (source used - County Borough of Dublin (Wards) (Amendment) Regulations, 1997). District electoral divisions and wards were both renamed to electoral divisions in 1996 via the Local Government Act 1994, hence the new "WARDORDED" attribute

items.label: Electoral Divisions 1997 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1997, assembled from Connacht (= 1996 boundaries), Leinster 1997, Munster (= 1996 boundaries), Ulster (= 1996 boundaries). items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 2019, assembled from Connacht (= 1996 boundaries), Leinster (= 1997 boundaries), Munster 2019, Ulster (= 1996 boundaries). items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1941 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1941-04-17, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster 1941, Munster (= 1921 boundaries), Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1942. In 1942, following the expansion of Dublin county borough, its new territory was transferred from Terenure DED to Crumlin ward.

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1942 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1942-04-23, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster 1942, Munster (= 1921 boundaries), Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1943. In 1943, following the addition of Howth Urban District to Dublin county borough, its territory was designated as a new 34th ward called Beann Eadair.

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1943 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1943-10-13, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster 1943, Munster (= 1921 boundaries), Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1944. In 1944, Waterford county borough’s boundary was expanded into the DEDs of Ballynakill, Kilbarry and Waterford Rural.

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1944 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1944-04-01, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster (= 1943 boundaries), Munster 1944, Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1946. In 1946, Dublin county borough’s existing 34 wards were replaced with 33 new wards.

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1946 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1946-07-15, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster 1946, Munster (= 1944 boundaries), Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1950. In 1950, the new DED of Limerick Rural was formed out of parts of Limerick North Rural and Limerick South Rural due to the forthcoming expansion of Limerick county borough. Also relevant is the renaming of the following DEDs between 1936 Census Reports Volume 1 (published 1938) and 1946 Census Reports Volume 1 (published 1949): Edgeworthstown to Meathas Truim (Longford), Drumcondra to Drumconrath (Meath), Philipstown to Daingean (Offaly), Charleville to Rathluirc (Cork), Shanballymore to Shanballymore Town (Cork)

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1950 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1950-01-05, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster (= 1949 boundaries), Munster 1950, Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1953. In 1953, Dublin county borough's boundary was expanded into the DEDs of Castleknock, Clondalkin, Coolock, Drumcondra Rural, Finglas, Howth Rural, Palmerstown, Rathfarnham and Terenure.

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1953 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1953-04-01, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster 1953, Munster (= 1950 boundaries), Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1954. In 1954, following the expansion of Dublin county borough in 1953, 9 new wards replaced the portions of 9 DEDs (Castleknock, Clondalkin, Coolock, Drumcondra Rural, Finglas, Howth Rural, Palmerstown, Rathfarnham and Terenure) that had become part of the county borough. Minor boundary changes were made to some of the 33 existing wards (making a total of 42).

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1954 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1954-06-14, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster 1954, Munster (= 1950 boundaries), Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1955. In 1955, Cork county borough's boundary expanded into the DEDs of Bishopstown, St. Mary's and Blackrock and Waterford county borough’s boundary was expanded further into the DEDs of Ballynakill and Waterford Rural as well as the DED of Kilculliheen in County Kilkenny.

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1955 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1955-04-01, assembled from Connacht (= 1919 boundaries), Leinster (= 1954 boundaries), Munster 1955, Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1957. In 1957, due to the forthcoming expansion of Bray, part of the DED of Rathmichael was transferred from County Dublin to County Wicklow and became its own DED called Rathmichael (Bray).

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1957 source files
items.description: Republic of Ireland District Electoral Divisions/Wards as at 1957-11-01, assembled from Connacht 1957, Leinster 1957, Munster 1957, Ulster (= 1921 boundaries). Modified version of District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1965. In 1965, Cork county borough's boundary expanded further into the DEDs of Bishopstown, St. Mary's and Blackrock (the last of which it fully absorbed). Also relevant is the renaming of the following DEDs between 1951 Census Reports Volume 1 (published 1952) and 1956 Census Reports Volume 1 (published 1957): Bagenalstown Rural to Muinebeag Rural (Carlow), Bagenalstown Urban to Muinebeag Urban (Carlow), Newbridge Rural to Droichead Nua Rural (Kildare), Newbridge Urban to Droichead Nua Urban (Kildare), Maryborough Rural to Portlaoighise Rural (Laois), Maryborough Urban to Portlaoighise Urban (Laois), Navan Rural to An Uaimh Rural (Meath), Navan Urban to An Uaimh Urban (Meath), WKells Rural to Ceanannas Mór Rural (Meath), Kells Urban to Ceanannas Mór Urban (Meath), Drumconrath to Drumcondra (Meath), Rosbercon to Rosbercon Urban (Wexford), Shanballymore Town to Shanballymore (Cork), Binghamstown North to An Geata Mór Thuaidh (Mayo), Binghamstown South to An Geata Mór Theas (Mayo)

items.label: District Electoral Divisions/Wards 1965 source files

Also relevant is the renaming of the following DEDs between 1956 Census Reports Volume 1 (published 1957) and 1961 Census Reports Volume 1 (published 1963): Frankford to Kilcormac (Offaly), Mountcharles to Tantallon (Donegal)

items.label: Tellus Rural Soil (A Horizon — Aqua Regia Digest) source files
items.description: A-horizon (topsoil) samples from the Tellus rural soil survey digested with aqua regia and analysed for the trace/heavy metal elements that resist XRF. Complements the A-horizon XRF layer. ~6,870 points.

items.label: Tellus Rural Soil Survey (A Soils, XRF) source files
items.description: Topsoil ("A horizon") samples collected on a 2 km grid across rural Northern Ireland under the Tellus survey and analysed by XRF. Approximately 6,860 points.

items.label: Tellus Rural Soil (S Horizon — Aqua Regia Digest) source files
items.description: S-horizon (subsoil) samples from the Tellus rural soil survey, aqua regia digest. The deeper soil samples — useful for distinguishing surface anthropogenic contamination from underlying geology. ~6,870 points.

items.label: Tellus Rural Soil (S Horizon — Fire Assay for Au and PGE) source files
items.description: S-horizon subsoil samples subjected to fire assay specifically to recover gold (Au) and platinum group elements. The classical mineral-prospecting technique applied across the Tellus survey grid. ~6,850 points.

items.label: Tellus Rural Soil (S Horizon — Near-Total Digest) source files
items.description: S-horizon (subsoil) samples digested with HF-HClO4-HNO3 ("near total") and analysed by ICP-MS — a more aggressive extraction than aqua regia, recovering more of the silicate-bound element pool. ~6,870 points.

items.label: Tellus Stream Sediments (Gold and Platinum Group Elements) source files
items.description: Tellus stream-sediment samples assayed specifically for gold (Au) and platinum group elements (PGE — Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Os, Ir). ~5,690 sample points.

items.label: Tellus Stream Sediments (Boron) source files
items.description: Tellus stream-sediment samples specifically analysed for boron, which requires a separate analytical method from the main XRF panel. ~5,840 points.

items.label: Tellus Stream Sediments (Regional XRF) source files
items.description: Regional stream-sediment samples collected under the Tellus survey, analysed by XRF for major and trace elements. Approximately 5,800 sample points across Northern Ireland.

items.label: Tellus Stream Sediments (Regional XRF — Set 2) source files
items.description: Second set of regional stream-sediment samples (Tellus survey), analysed by XRF for an additional suite of major and trace elements beyond the Set 1 panel. ~5,870 points.

items.label: Tellus Stream Waters (Regional ICP) source files
items.description: Regional stream-water samples collected under the Tellus survey, analysed by ICP-MS for dissolved elements. Approximately 5,900 sample points.

items.label: OSNI Benchmarks (Height Reference Points) source files
items.description: Historic OSNI benchmarks — small brass plates or chiselled grooves set into permanent features (bridges, walls, milestones) whose heights above Ordnance Datum were precisely determined by levelling surveys. Used by surveyors as known reference points before GPS. ~10,000 points across Northern Ireland, each attributed with its height in metres.

items.label: OSNI River Basin LiDAR — Stonyford (2014, 1 m hillshade) source files
items.description: Multidirectional hillshade of the 1 m bare-earth LiDAR digital terrain model (DTM) for the Stonyford catchment, flown 2014 in the OSNI/LPS River Basin LiDAR survey. Reveals fine ground topography — stream channels, field drains, banks and earthworks — beneath vegetation.

items.label: OSNI Historical Six-Inch Maps — Edition 1 (1829–1835) source files
items.description: The original Six-Inch-to-One-Mile County Series — the first complete topographic survey of Ireland, produced 1829–1835 by the Ordnance Survey. 308 historical map sheets covering all six Northern Ireland counties (Antrim, Armagh, Derry/Londonderry, Down, Fermanagh, Tyrone), engraved at a scale where every individual building, road, field boundary, and town feature is shown. Mosaicked and re-tiled here at 4 m/pixel for interactive viewing on the catalogue map. For pixel-level detail, download the original sheet TIFs from the per-county packages linked below.

items.label: OSNI Historical Six-Inch Maps — Edition 2 (1838–1862) source files
items.description: Second edition of the Six-Inch-to-One-Mile County Series, surveyed 1838–1862, providing the first comprehensive update to the original 1830s survey. 261 historical sheets covering all six Northern Ireland counties. Captures the rapid changes in Irish landscape, settlement patterns, and infrastructure during the mid-19th century — including the period before, during, and immediately after the Great Famine (1845–1852). Mosaicked and re-tiled here at 4 m/pixel.

items.label: OSNI StreetMaps — Town Sheets source files
items.description: Detailed printed street-map sheets for 109 towns and villages across Northern Ireland — 0.85 m/pixel native resolution showing individual streets, building outlines, and town features. Coverage is sparse (only published towns are mapped); the rest of NI is blank in this layer. Served as XYZ tiles at zoom 8–16.

items.label: Tellus Electromagnetic — 14 kHz Apparent Conductivity source files
items.description: Apparent ground conductivity at 14 kHz — shallower depth (~10–30 m) than the 3 kHz channel, more sensitive to surface and near-surface conductors. Useful for soil moisture, near-surface alteration, and thin clay layers. Viridis colormap, -2σ to +4σ stretch.

items.label: Tellus Electromagnetic — 3 kHz Apparent Conductivity source files
items.description: Apparent ground conductivity at 3 kHz from the Tellus airborne EM survey — penetrates ~50–150 m, mapping conductive saline groundwater, clay-rich soils, mineralised zones, and pollution plumes. Viridis colormap (low = purple, high = yellow), -2σ to +4σ stretch.

items.label: Tellus Electromagnetic — raw airborne flight-line data source files
items.description: Raw multi-frequency airborne EM coil readings along each Tellus flight line — the original point measurements behind the gridded conductivity products. Frequencies 912 Hz, 3 kHz, 11.9 kHz, and 24.5 kHz at the same line/sample spacing as the magnetic data.

items.label: Tellus Airborne Survey — Flight Lines source files
items.description: The actual flight-line pattern flown by the Tellus airborne geophysical survey (2005–2008) — 2 210 individual flight lines at ~250 m spacing across all of Northern Ireland, derived from the raw radiometric sample positions. Toggle on alongside any of the gridded magnetic / electromagnetic / radiometric layers to see where the survey actually sampled the ground; anomalies on the gridded products are most reliable inside dense flight coverage and progressively less reliable on the edges and in gaps. Single inert MultiLineString — non-interactive (no per-line popup, hover, or click) so it doesn't compete with the per-feature data layers underneath.

items.label: Tellus Magnetic — raw airborne flight-line data source files
items.description: Raw magnetometer readings along each Tellus survey flight line — the original point measurements that the gridded "Tellus Magnetic" products on this site are derived from. Typically ~250 m line spacing with samples every ~7 m. Useful only if you want to re-grid with custom parameters or interrogate noise; for a map-style view use the gridded TMI / RTP / RTP-Tilt cards in this category.

items.label: Tellus Magnetic — Reduction-to-Pole (RTP) source files
items.description: TMI corrected by reduction-to-pole, which compensates for the dipolar shape of magnetic anomalies caused by NI's inclined magnetic field. RTP places the peak directly above the source body, simplifying interpretation. ±3σ rainbow ramp.

items.label: Tellus Magnetic — RTP Tilt Derivative source files
items.description: Tilt derivative of the RTP magnetic field — an edge-detection filter that highlights the boundaries of magnetic source bodies regardless of their amplitude. Excellent for tracing dykes, faults, and contacts. ±3σ rainbow ramp.

items.label: Tellus Magnetic — Total Magnetic Intensity (residual) source files
items.description: Residual total magnetic intensity (TMI) from the GSNI Tellus airborne survey — variations in the Earth's magnetic field caused by buried magnetic minerals (chiefly magnetite). High-magnetic anomalies trace mafic/ultramafic intrusions, basaltic flows, and iron-bearing sedimentary basins; magnetic lows mark sedimentary basins and demagnetised alteration zones. 35m grid spacing, ±3σ rainbow ramp.

items.label: Tellus Radiometric — Potassium (K %) source files
items.description: Surface potassium concentration from natural gamma-ray emissions. Highlights granites and other felsic intrusions (potassium-rich), alkaline volcanics, and certain sedimentary horizons. Inferno colormap (dark = low, bright = high), ±2-3σ stretch.

items.label: Tellus Radiometric — raw airborne flight-line data source files
items.description: Raw airborne gamma-ray spectrometer readings along each Tellus flight line — K, U, Th window counts plus total count, before gridding into the radiometric maps already on this site. Useful for re-processing or quality-assessing the gridded products.

items.label: Tellus Radiometric — K/Th/U Ternary RGB source files
items.description: The iconic radiometric ternary composite — K mapped to red, Th to green, U to blue. Reds = potassic (granite, certain volcanics); greens = thorium-rich (resistate sediments, heavy minerals); blues = uranium-rich (organic shales, mineralisation); whites/pale = high in all three; blacks = low overall. The most interpretively powerful single radiometric view. Each band stretched independently to mean ± 2σ.

items.label: Tellus Radiometric — Thorium-Equivalent (eTh ppm) source files
items.description: Thorium-equivalent concentration from the 2.61 MeV thallium-208 daughter peak. Often correlates with heavy minerals (monazite, zircon) in placer deposits and resistate sediments. Rainbow colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.

items.label: Tellus Radiometric — Total Counts (gamma) source files
items.description: Total gamma-ray count rate — a summed proxy for combined K, U, Th, and other radionuclide activity. Useful for identifying overall radiometric "hot" zones before decomposing into individual channels. Inferno colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.

items.label: Tellus Radiometric — Uranium-Equivalent (eU ppm) source files
items.description: Uranium-equivalent concentration from the 1.76 MeV bismuth-214 daughter peak. Highlights uranium-bearing granites, organic-rich shales, phosphatic horizons, and mineralised zones. Viridis colormap, ±2-3σ stretch.

items.label: Agricultural Critical Risk Areas (DAERA) source files
items.description: DAERA classification of land parcels by their relative risk of contributing diffuse agricultural pollution to receiving waters. Each parcel is scored 0–1 (`riskscore2`) by combining slope, hydrological connectivity, soil characteristics, rainfall, river-buffer proximity and land-use rules. Companion to the Network Contribution datasets — the polygon equivalent of the per-river-basin SciMAP score.

items.label: DAERA Network Contribution — SciMAP modelled pollution scores by river basin (26 catchments) source files
items.description: Per-river-basin pollution-contribution scores from the SciMAP hydrological model (CEH Land Cover 2007 + Met Office rainfall + 5 m DTM), rasterised at 25 m and rendered as a Web Mercator tile pyramid coloured on inferno (low → high contribution). Raw GRIDCODE values of 58–100 stretch the inferno ramp from dark purple to pale yellow. Each parcel of land is scored for how much sediment / nutrient pollution its upstream catchment contributes to receiving waters. 26 catchment datasets were rasterised individually, mosaicked, and re-projected; per-catchment download links remain in sourceDownloads for the raw vector data.

items.label: River Water Quality Monitoring 1990–2018 (14 chemistry parameters) source files
items.description: Long-term chemistry time-series from NI rivers, 1990–2018, broken down by 14 individual parameters (pH, dissolved oxygen, BOD, ammonia, nitrate, nitrite, dissolved iron, suspended solids, plus extended set: alkalinity, conductivity, dissolved copper, dissolved zinc, soluble phosphorus). The "umbrella" package contains the spatial monitoring sites + summary; per-parameter packages contain the full time-series CSVs. No interactive map layer — use the WFD Monitoring Sites layer to see where samples are taken.
